situation.summary: Tenant Perrin Dall reported on 4 Sep 2025 that the bathroom sash window will not open, the bedroom sash will not lock, and keys are missing (later clarified as no kitchen sash key, and mould in the bathroom). The landlord, Sella Marr, authorised the agency to use its own provider with no spending limit or detailed scope (E003). The provider changed twice: Hearthline Access (Tarin Vale) was removed on 11 Sep, and Keypath Repairs (Edrin Moss) took over. Keypath could not gain access on three attempts, collected no management keys, and gave no visit dates (E022). On 22 and 24 Sep Keypath said the work was completed on Friday 19 Sep, with an invoice to follow. On 25 Sep Keypath said the invoice would come "later today". No attendance record, visit notes, completion evidence or invoice is on file, and the tenant has not confirmed the work. The tenant's 14 Sep request for management keys has had no reply to the tenant.
situation.task: Verify the 'completed' claim before anything is closed or charged: ask the tenant (Perrin Dall) to confirm whether work was done and whether the locks and windows now work, and answer the open key request; in the same turn, ask Keypath (Edrin Moss) for the attendance record and completion evidence.
situation.stageLabel: Contractor reports work complete (19 Sep); tenant confirmation, attendance evidence and invoice outstanding
situation.whoseMove: The tenant is the first party we are waiting on, and we owe them a reply. Perrin Dall's 14 Sep request for management keys (E019) has never been answered directly, and nothing has been sent to the tenant since 11 Sep (E014). We need Perrin to confirm whether anyone attended around 19 Sep and whether the bedroom window locks, the bathroom window opens, and a kitchen key exists. Keypath (Edrin Moss) is also due to send the invoice "later today" (25 Sep, not yet passed at the snapshot), but it should be asked for the visit record now, because the invoice alone is not evidence of attendance. The landlord has not been told that the work is complete and should not be told yet. Proposed next action: tenant.ask by email to Perrin Dall, with a phone follow-up if there is no reply by Monday 29 Sep at 12:00, plus contractor.update to Edrin Moss by email asking for the visit record. Nothing should be closed or sent to the landlord until the tenant confirms.

decision.actionLabel: Ask the tenant, Perrin Dall, whether Keypath attended and whether each window lock and key issue is now fixed, and reply to the 14 September management-key question
decision.message:
Dear Perrin,

I'm sorry we didn't reply directly to your email of 14 September about using the management keys. We passed your request to our contractor, Keypath Repairs, that same day.

Keypath has told us by phone that they finished the window lock work on Friday 19 September. We have no visit record or report from them yet, so before we treat the job as finished we need you to confirm what happened. Could you please reply by Monday 29 September and tell us:

1. Did anyone from Keypath Repairs come to the flat on or around 19 September? If so, roughly when, and were you in?
2. Does the bedroom sash window now lock?
3. Does the bathroom sash window now open, and do its locking buttons work?
4. Do you now have a working key for the kitchen sash window?
5. Is the mould you mentioned in the bathroom still there?

If anything is still not working, tell us which item and we will arrange for it to be dealt with. If at any point a window cannot be secured and you cannot lock up safely, please call the office straight away rather than waiting to reply.

I will contact you again on Monday 29 September if we haven't heard from you by then.

Kind regards,
Ilyra Venn
Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings
decision.rationale: Keypath says the work was done on 19 September (E023, E025), but the only evidence is their word by phone. On 17 September they said they had tried three times, never found the tenant in and had not collected management keys (E022). The file has no appointment, attendance record or invoice (E024). Under the manual, when the only evidence is the contractor's word, we ask the tenant to confirm the fix. The tenant is also owed a reply: they asked about management keys on 14 September (E019) and have heard nothing from us since 11 September (E014). The invoice Keypath promised 'later today' (E025) is not due yet, so we should not chase it. Asking Keypath for its visit record is a new question, not a chase, so it can go in the same turn. The landlord should not be told the work is complete until there is evidence.
decision.expectedOutcome: The tenant confirms whether anyone attended and whether each item works. Combined with Keypath's visit record and invoice, this tells us whether to update the landlord and forward the invoice, or to get Keypath back to finish the work.
boundaries: The contractor saying the work is done does not prove it was done; nothing is confirmed until the tenant or a visit record confirms it.
Asking does not promise a date for any further visit or for management-key access.
The landlord is not told the work is complete, and no invoice is approved or forwarded, by this step.
Mould is asked about only to record its current state; this step does not decide whether it is in scope or who pays.
remainingWork: Receive Keypath's invoice, due 'later today' on 25 September; check the amount and VAT basis before forwarding.
Once completion is evidenced, update the landlord with what was done and the invoice; the landlord approved the work with no price or spending limit.
If the tenant reports items not fixed, or no visit at all, take it up with Keypath and consider escalating.
Take the bathroom mould to the landlord as a separate item if it is still present.
Confirm where the management keys are before closing.
assumptions: Email is the right channel for the tenant, as used throughout the case.
25 September 2025 is a Thursday, so Monday 29 September is two working days later.
Keypath had the tenant's details through the job forwarding (E018, E020).
